newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE volumes push higher in September.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE volumes push higher in September.

text.p: The London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) said on Wednesday that 14.1 million contracts were traded last month, the highest ever volume for the month of September.
The volume was 12 percent up on September 1995 levels, LIFFE said in a statement.
For the year to date, LIFFE volumes were 122.57 million contracts, up 19 percent on the same period last year, it said.
The average daily volume for September 1996 was 677,257 futures and options contracts, representing an average daily nominal value of 161 billion stg.
Since the merger of LIFFE and the London Commodity Exchange (LCE) on September 16 1996, LIFFE's Commodity Products has traded 139,234 contracts with an average daily volume of 12,658.

"Increased focus on European Monetary Union, together with greater volatility following Italian budgetary announcements has led to the busiest September ever at LIFFE," said Daniel Hodson, chief executive of LIFFE in a statement.

Three-month Eurolira interest rate futures set a new daily record of September 27 of 81,628 contracts, beating the May 1994 record of 65,986. They also set a new monthly record of 717,438, narrowly beating the July 1996 record of 717,253 contracts.
Options on three-month Eurolira contracts set a new daily record on September 27, trading 22,750 and breaking the previous daily record of 21,635 set on September 19, LIFFE said.
The contract set a new monthly record of 158,928 traded.
Options on Italian government bond (BTP) futures set a new daily record of 38,119 on September 27, beating the February 1994 record of 37,542.
